请分析我按输入顺序提供的 1–6 张角色参考图，生成用于替换 H3 通用模板中 {{CHARACTER_PROFILES}} 的英文角色描述。

这里的 Character 指目标角色，不限定为人类：真人、3D 玩偶、毛绒角色、卡通形象、拟人动物、机器人和吉祥物等均适用。按参考图判断角色类别，不把非人类角色默认描述成 woman、man 或 realistically proportioned human。

只输出实际提供角色的描述，不加解释，不输出未提供图片的占位条目。每张图应明确一个目标角色；若某张图含多个角色且未指定目标，请先问清目标，不擅自新增角色编号。

固定对应关系：
Character 1：<Picture 1>，对应视频蓝色 BLUE 源动作角色。
Character 2：<Picture 2>，对应视频红色 RED 源动作角色。
Character 3：<Picture 3>，对应视频绿色 GREEN 源动作角色。
Character 4：<Picture 4>，对应视频品红色 MAGENTA 源动作角色。
Character 5：<Picture 5>，对应视频青色 CYAN 源动作角色。
Character 6：<Picture 6>，对应视频黄色 YELLOW 源动作角色。

每个实际角色单独写一段英文，建议 80–140 个英文单词。按实际提供的图片，使用对应角色的完整英文段首：

Character 1 is the target character in <Picture 1>, assigned to the BLUE source performer.

Character 2 is the target character in <Picture 2>, assigned to the RED source performer.

Character 3 is the target character in <Picture 3>, assigned to the GREEN source performer.

Character 4 is the target character in <Picture 4>, assigned to the MAGENTA source performer.

Character 5 is the target character in <Picture 5>, assigned to the CYAN source performer.

Character 6 is the target character in <Picture 6>, assigned to the YELLOW source performer.

以上六句是对应角色的段首规则，不代表必须输出六个角色。只使用实际提供图片对应的句子，并在该句后继续写该角色的外观和比例描述；未提供的角色整段省略。

然后描述该角色图片里可见的固定设计：角色类别、视觉风格、身份特征、主体宽度相对高度、轮廓、各部分大小关系，以及实际具有的头部、躯干、四肢或其它结构的比例；补充材质、颜色、毛发、服装、鞋子及配饰等可见特征。没有的身体结构和服装不写，不为了凑字数编造人类的脸、手、脚或关节。

各角色分别描述，不平均体型。即使多张图的脸或外形相似，也保留每个角色独立的造型、材质及已有服饰。忠实保留 3D 玩偶或卡通角色的非标准比例、夸张结构和原始渲染风格，不默认写实，不改成人类标准体型。区分头部本体与耳朵、角、帽子等附属结构；区分衣服外轮廓与实际可见身体。无法看清的部位不要编造，不虚构精确比例数字，不把宽松服装解释为身体肥胖。

不描述参考图站姿、当前动作、镜头、背景或光线，不写剧情。不把蓝、红、绿、品红、青、黄这些动作标识颜色加入目标角色的身体表面、毛发、材质或衣服，除非参考图本身确实有该颜色。

<Video 1> 是本次片段的深度动作参考。以它的原始时间顺序和节奏为准，复刻身体、头部、手臂、手掌及手指的运动；完整保留动作幅度很小的阶段和停顿，不省略、压缩、加速或提前进入后续动作。动作的发生时刻与持续时间由参考视频决定，不另编舞。 严格按参考视频每一帧的先后顺序，在对应的时间复现其姿态和连续变化；即使相邻帧动作很小或姿态基本不变，也完整保留这一阶段的持续时间，不跳帧概括动作、不提前执行后面的动作、不重新排列动作、不自行增加动作或加快节奏。

参考视频只用于身体动作、头部姿态和动作节奏控制，不是最终画面内容。输出保持<Picture 1>的正常彩色写实外观，不出现灰色深度、点线、网格、字幕或新增镜头。

Each entry identifies a target reference image and its assigned source performer. That current image alone defines identity, appearance, physique, original dimensions, proportions, materials and existing outfit. These descriptions apply to the respective character, not the background. No character category or setting is fixed by this template. Pose and expression may change with the assigned performance; visible image features override conflicting written descriptions.
<Subject 2> is only the assigned body action, facial performance and observable mouth states in <Video 1>, including movement and stillness at their original times.
<Subject 3> is the actual visible background of the user-designated reference picture, or the first supplied reference picture by default. Its empty areas and absence of scenery are part of the reference, not space to decorate.
<Video 1> supplies performance only. Its marked characters provide actions, expressions and mouth shapes, not target appearance, body build, body size, proportions, background, lighting, style, composition or camera behaviour. Source identifiers indicate performance ownership only. Verified original audio, when supplied, adds a mouth-timing reference; soundtrack reuse requires a separate request.

summary:
[reference generation] Animate the original image-defined <Subject 1> inside the image-defined <Subject 3>. Transfer only the assigned performance from <Subject 2>, preserving its changes and stillness at the original times, and retaining each target's appearance, physique, dimensions and proportions.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - retain each target's own identity, appearance, physique, size relationships, proportions, style, materials and existing outfit.
<Subject 2>: attribute_transfer - transfer assigned action, expression, gaze, observed mouth state, head coupling, interaction role and timing without adding performance.
<Subject 3>: fully_preserved - retain the selected picture's actual background content, empty areas, surfaces, existing objects, lighting and visual style without adding environmental content.
<Video 1>: fully_preserved - preserve only its defined performance role; exclude all other source visual information.

detailed_description:
Generate exactly the configured image characters in <Subject 3>.
[Shot 1] Begin directly in the assigned source action phase, expression and readable mouth state, adapted to the target's original body and face. Add no preparation interval or transition from the picture's pose.

Read the background from the currently selected reference picture, preserving its actual content, surfaces, lighting and visual treatment. Retain existing scenery when shown and preserve empty regions when none is shown. Do not add environmental content or infer a setting from a character's clothing, identity, era or story. With different image backgrounds, use the designated picture or the first by default as one shared scene. Do not adopt the video's environment or camera. If panels depict alternate views of the same individual, they describe that target rather than additional cast members; do not reproduce panel dividers or repeated views.

Preserve each target's image-defined facial identity, hair or other surface features, body build, original width relative to height, head-to-body ratio, torso shape, limb lengths and thicknesses, and hand or foot sizes where present. Retain its original dimensions and size relationships to visible image-based scene cues. Do not enlarge, miniaturize, slim, bulk up, stretch or compress it to fit a source performer. Do not equalize different characters' heights or average their physiques. A toy, doll, cartoon or nonhuman character retains its original structure, materials and expressive features rather than acquiring human anatomy.

Frame the picture-derived scene to fit the cast's full movement range from the beginning, including raised limbs, feet, garment hems and existing appendages or accessories. Keep complete silhouettes visible except for requested exits. Widen the view or adjust staging when needed without changing scene identity, body dimensions or relative character scales. Do not deform or independently resize bodies, enlarge the centre character, crop side characters or add close-ups. Perspective may change projected size naturally; source screen sizes and composition do not define target sizes.

Reconstruct every assigned performer as the complete image-defined target. Its entire visible head, face, body, appendages, surfaces, outfit, footwear and accessories belong to that target design. Leave no source mannequin, exposed reference body, surface coating, leftover limbs or target-head/source-body mixture. Source markings never become target appearance.

Keep every supplied assignment through turning, crossing, occlusion and changes of source screen position. Each gesture, expression, gaze, mouth movement, hold or pause affects only the assigned target. Preserve independent performances without exchanging identities, outfits, body parts or action streams.

Retarget joint movement, orientation, coordination, support changes, locomotion and interaction timing to each unchanged target structure. Adapt reach, contact and staging to its own anatomy and the image-derived scene. Match the action rather than source screen coordinates, skeleton dimensions or body outline. Keep bodies and appendages distinct during overlaps.

Match only observed facial changes in brows, eyelids, blinks, gaze, cheeks, lips, jaw and head, including their intensity, asymmetry, holds and release. Keep unchanged areas still and preserve the target's facial identity and existing structures. Body movement alone does not imply speech, laughter, gasping or an open jaw.

Copy the assigned source's visible mouth state at each corresponding time: closed, slightly parted, open or still. Keep visibly closed lips closed for the full source interval; retain a slight gap when the source is only slightly parted, without increasing its opening. Match upper- and lower-lip contours, lip corners, jaw, closures, holds and head coupling on the target's own design. Show teeth or tongue only when present in its anatomy and clearly supported by source frames. No extra jaw cycles, speech gestures or opening through source closures; another performer must not drive this mouth.

An unreadable mouth or mesh shadow is not evidence of opening. Add no articulation in uncertain regions; retain the last reliable state when continuity supports it, otherwise use a restrained resting state consistent with the target image. Do not override clearly visible source evidence with invented opening or forced closure.

When verified original audio is actually supplied, check the visible source mouth states against its real openings, closures, sustained sounds, pauses, breaths and stress over the full duration. During silence, close the lips or retain the actual source state. Known dialogue must not replace the source timeline. Never guess character, syllable or phoneme intervals; use phoneme timing only from a reliable alignment tool. Without usable audio, follow readable visual mouth states only; no audio synchronization anchor exists.

At target time t, follow the assigned performance phase at the same elapsed source time t. Preserve onset, peak, hold, release, rest and completion without added delay. Align frame rates by elapsed time, not equal frame numbers. Do not retime or extend performance beyond source coverage.

Let existing garments and accessories respond naturally while retaining their image-defined design and fit. Keep the picture-derived environment and stable ensemble framing consistent. Add no test markers, comparison panels, reference layouts or extra characters.

overall_soundscape:
Do not invent speech or vocalizations from mouth movement. Reuse verified source speech only when its actual soundtrack is supplied and reuse is requested, preserving original words and timing. Without usable audio, do not fabricate it. Add ambience only if requested.

<Subject 1> is the target cast defined below, with only the characters needed for this generation:
Character 1 is the target character in <Picture 1>, assigned to the BLUE source performer. This character is a live-action figure depicting a stylized pig-like persona. The





Each entry identifies a target reference image and its assigned source performer. That current image alone defines identity, appearance, physique, original dimensions, proportions, materials and existing outfit. These descriptions apply to the respective character, not the background. No character category or setting is fixed by this template. Pose and expression may change with the assigned performance; visible image features override conflicting written descriptions.
<Subject 2> is only the assigned body action, facial performance and observable mouth states in <Video 1>, including movement and stillness at their original times.
<Subject 3> is the actual visible background of the user-designated reference picture, or the first supplied reference picture by default. Its empty areas and absence of scenery are part of the reference, not space to decorate.
<Video 1> supplies performance only. Its marked characters provide actions, expressions and mouth shapes, not target appearance, body build, body size, proportions, background, lighting, style, composition or camera behaviour. Source identifiers indicate performance ownership only. Verified original audio, when supplied, adds a mouth-timing reference; soundtrack reuse requires a separate request.

summary:
[reference generation] Animate the original image-defined <Subject 1> inside the image-defined <Subject 3>. Transfer only the assigned performance from <Subject 2>, preserving its changes and stillness at the original times, and retaining each target's appearance, physique, dimensions and proportions.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1>: fully_preserved - retain each target's own identity, appearance, physique, size relationships, proportions, style, materials and existing outfit.
<Subject 2>: attribute_transfer - transfer assigned action, expression, gaze, observed mouth state, head coupling, interaction role and timing without adding performance.
<Subject 3>: fully_preserved - retain the selected picture's actual background content, empty areas, surfaces, existing objects, lighting and visual style without adding environmental content.
<Video 1>: fully_preserved - preserve only its defined performance role; exclude all other source visual information.

detailed_description:
Generate exactly the configured image characters in <Subject 3>.
[Shot 1] Begin directly in the assigned source action phase, expression and readable mouth state, adapted to the target's original body and face. Add no preparation interval or transition from the picture's pose.

Read the background from the currently selected reference picture, preserving its actual content, surfaces, lighting and visual treatment. Retain existing scenery when shown and preserve empty regions when none is shown. Do not add environmental content or infer a setting from a character's clothing, identity, era or story. With different image backgrounds, use the designated picture or the first by default as one shared scene. Do not adopt the video's environment or camera. If panels depict alternate views of the same individual, they describe that target rather than additional cast members; do not reproduce panel dividers or repeated views.

Preserve each target's image-defined facial identity, hair or other surface features, body build, original width relative to height, head-to-body ratio, torso shape, limb lengths and thicknesses, and hand or foot sizes where present. Retain its original dimensions and size relationships to visible image-based scene cues. Do not enlarge, miniaturize, slim, bulk up, stretch or compress it to fit a source performer. Do not equalize different characters' heights or average their physiques. A toy, doll, cartoon or nonhuman character retains its original structure, materials and expressive features rather than acquiring human anatomy.

Frame the picture-derived scene to fit the cast's full movement range from the beginning, including raised limbs, feet, garment hems and existing appendages or accessories. Keep complete silhouettes visible except for requested exits. Widen the view or adjust staging when needed without changing scene identity, body dimensions or relative character scales. Do not deform or independently resize bodies, enlarge the centre character, crop side characters or add close-ups. Perspective may change projected size naturally; source screen sizes and composition do not define target sizes.

Reconstruct every assigned performer as the complete image-defined target. Its entire visible head, face, body, appendages, surfaces, outfit, footwear and accessories belong to that target design. Leave no source mannequin, exposed reference body, surface coating, leftover limbs or target-head/source-body mixture. Source markings never become target appearance.

Keep every supplied assignment through turning, crossing, occlusion and changes of source screen position. Each gesture, expression, gaze, mouth movement, hold or pause affects only the assigned target. Preserve independent performances without exchanging identities, outfits, body parts or action streams.

Retarget joint movement, orientation, coordination, support changes, locomotion and interaction timing to each unchanged target structure. Adapt reach, contact and staging to its own anatomy and the image-derived scene. Match the action rather than source screen coordinates, skeleton dimensions or body outline. Keep bodies and appendages distinct during overlaps.

Match only observed facial changes in brows, eyelids, blinks, gaze, cheeks, lips, jaw and head, including their intensity, asymmetry, holds and release. Keep unchanged areas still and preserve the target's facial identity and existing structures. Body movement alone does not imply speech, laughter, gasping or an open jaw.

Copy the assigned source's visible mouth state at each corresponding time: closed, slightly parted, open or still. Keep visibly closed lips closed for the full source interval; retain a slight gap when the source is only slightly parted, without increasing its opening. Match upper- and lower-lip contours, lip corners, jaw, closures, holds and head coupling on the target's own design. Show teeth or tongue only when present in its anatomy and clearly supported by source frames. No extra jaw cycles, speech gestures or opening through source closures; another performer must not drive this mouth.

An unreadable mouth or mesh shadow is not evidence of opening. Add no articulation in uncertain regions; retain the last reliable state when continuity supports it, otherwise use a restrained resting state consistent with the target image. Do not override clearly visible source evidence with invented opening or forced closure.

When verified original audio is actually supplied, check the visible source mouth states against its real openings, closures, sustained sounds, pauses, breaths and stress over the full duration. During silence, close the lips or retain the actual source state. Known dialogue must not replace the source timeline. Never guess character, syllable or phoneme intervals; use phoneme timing only from a reliable alignment tool. Without usable audio, follow readable visual mouth states only; no audio synchronization anchor exists.

At target time t, follow the assigned performance phase at the same elapsed source time t. Preserve onset, peak, hold, release, rest and completion without added delay. Align frame rates by elapsed time, not equal frame numbers. Do not retime or extend performance beyond source coverage.

Let existing garments and accessories respond naturally while retaining their image-defined design and fit. Keep the picture-derived environment and stable ensemble framing consistent. Add no test markers, comparison panels, reference layouts or extra characters.

overall_soundscape:
Do not invent speech or vocalizations from mouth movement. Reuse verified source speech only when its actual soundtrack is supplied and reuse is requested, preserving original words and timing. Without usable audio, do not fabricate it. Add ambience only if requested.

properties.text:
1-参考图尽量是人物全身正面照（本地int8模型跑的话），后期测试发现本地注意力不够，画面会乱
2-现目前是通用的提示词模板，我修改测试了好几个版本，但是不保证稳定性强！适合简单的动作迁移！最好的方式就是把白模的视频丢给agent，并说好一一对应的角色颜色去做H3的提示词，高动态的让agent去拆视频对帧去写！
3-通用模板的提示词抽卡率比较高，说到抽卡这个事，大家一定要有心理准备哈，别跑一两次觉得效果不行，就死犟！多抽抽卡呀，一张图片效果不好你还抽个十几二十次呢！

widgets_values:
| 选项 | 适合什么情况 |
|---|---|
| **高／超高** | 常规 AI 放大，建议先用 |
| **降噪低～超高** | 去噪点、压缩杂质；强度过高可能磨皮 |
| **去模糊低～超高** | 改善画面发糊；过强可能出现锐化边缘 |
| **高比特率高／超高** | 原片已经清晰、压缩少，希望放大时保留纹理 |
| **流式中／超高** | 直播、摄像头等流媒体素材 |
| **双三次插值** | 普通尺寸缩放，不做 AI 增强 |
